# Scikit-bio: a fundamental Python library for biological omic data analysis

- DOI: [10.1038/s41592-025-02981-z](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41592-025-02981-z)
- Official repository: <https://github.com/scikit-bio/scikit-bio>
- Catalog entry: `SCIKITBIO_2026`
- Local entrypoint: `python/17_scikit_bio_manifest.py`
- Current readiness: `manifest-only`

## Why this belongs in the workbench

A research project often mixes sequence files, feature tables, metadata, distances, taxonomies and phylogenetic trees. scikit-bio offers a common Python layer for biological data structures and algorithms, which makes it useful as a reproducible utility layer alongside the R-first methods in this collection.

It should be treated as a toolkit, not as a single end-to-end statistical method. The scientific question, experimental unit, null model and assay-specific preprocessing still belong to the project.

## Input contract

Record the following before choosing an API:

1. operation family: sequence, table, distance, diversity, taxonomy or phylogeny;
2. file formats and parser versions (FASTA/FASTQ, BIOM/TSV, Newick or other);
3. sequence, feature and sample identifiers and their join rules;
4. metadata fields, missingness and biological replicate;
5. distance metric, tree rooting and branch-length conventions where relevant;
6. statistical design, covariates, permutations and multiple-testing policy.

The catalog manifest records these choices without importing a package or silently converting formats.

```bash
python python/17_scikit_bio_manifest.py \
  --inputs data/real/reads.fasta data/real/metadata.tsv \
  --operation sequence \
  --format FASTA \
  --output results/scikit_bio_manifest.json
```

For a minimal smoke test:

```bash
python python/17_scikit_bio_manifest.py \
  --inputs data/mock/narmbench_reference.fa \
  --operation sequence \
  --format FASTA
```

## Baseline and validation

- validate identifiers and metadata joins before computing distances or diversity;
- compare the selected operation with an assay-appropriate baseline;
- keep sample/donor as the unit of inference rather than treating sequences or features as independent biological replicates;
- preserve parser settings, distance/tree conventions, permutations, random seeds and software versions;
- inspect one small known example before scaling to the full dataset.

## Interpretation boundary

scikit-bio can make an operation and its data representation reproducible. It does not select the best assay, correct batch effects automatically, establish causality or turn a distance/phylogeny result into a mechanism.

## Reading output

- Claim to retain: the chosen operation can be reconstructed from the recorded formats, identifiers, metadata and parameters.
- Claim not to retain: a library result alone proves a biological mechanism or validates an experimental design.
- Next validation: rerun an assay-specific baseline and confirm the result at the correct sample/replicate level.
